plain: The story is that in 1945, in the weeks after the first atomic bomb test at the Trinity site in New Mexico, a craft crashed nearby, and Michels says a larger piece of strange material came from that crash. Michels raises it several times, in one episode citing the ufologist Jacques Vallée's then new book and giving the date as August 17, 1945, in another putting it 20 days after the July 1945 test, and once dating it to 1948 as one of a run of crashes near nuclear sites. Vallée tells it on the show second-hand, crediting it to people he names as Paola Harris, Remy Baca and Jose Padilla and to his book Trinity: The Best-Kept Secret: he places it near San Antonio, New Mexico, and says that through an opening where one panel was missing, the onlookers saw three creatures that were human-like, with two eyes. A researcher named Jason Jorjani, retelling Vallée's book, says the craft was bomb-shaped and that the Mexican locals who came across the beings said they looked like praying mantises, and a clip of an unnamed witness on the same episode describes them as "baldheaded," with slanted teardrop eyes and no ears. Another guest, Marik von Rennenkampff, mentions it only tentatively, saying there was "possibly" a crash at Trinity and that it is "unclear." If true, it would tie UFO crashes to the very start of the nuclear age.
